newsitem.title: UK: Centrica starts gas discount scheme.
newsitem.headline: Centrica starts gas discount scheme.

text.p: Centrica Plc, the gas supply arm spun off from British Gas last month, on Tuesday introduced a new price scheme which offers customers in the south west of England discounts of up to 12 percent on their bills.
The south west was the first area in Britain where competition was introduced in the domestic gas market. The market in the region was opened up in April 1996.
Centrica said it had launched its new ValuePlus scheme to fight off the aggressive marketing of competing suppliers.

Rivals such as major oil and gas companies and electricity firms have moved into the southwest region's gas market, undercutting Centrica prices by some 15 percent and luring away about 20 percent of the former monopoly's customers.

ValuePlus is available to customers who choose to pay by monthly direct debit and are prepared to stay with Centrica, which still markets its products under the British Gas brand name, for a minimum 12 months.

"We're committed to offering a value for money package of price and service which will make customers choose to stay with us," said Mike Alexander, managing director of Centrica's domestic trading business said. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
